key_insight: Microscopic residual impurities in wide-bandgap perovskite films trigger degradation at impurity-perovskite interfaces, and can be rapidly detected with imaging plus machine learning before devices fail.
engineering_relevance: The work provides a non-invasive, high-throughput pre-screening tool for perovskite solar cell manufacturing to flag unstable films early and improve scale-up reliability.
method: Nano-FTIR plus optical and scanning probe microscopy to chemically validate impurity locations
High-resolution reflected light microscopy for rapid, non-invasive film inspection
Machine learning image analysis to quantify impurity density within seconds
evidence_signal: Photo-stress experiments showed degradation starts at impurity interfaces, and films with higher impurity density exhibited faster early degradation, supporting impurity density as an early stability metric.
watch_item: The imaging classifier must be carefully calibrated to film composition and processing conditions to avoid false positives or missed impurity-driven failure sites.
paper_title: High-Throughput Imaging of Degradation-Inducing Microscopic Impurities in Perovskite Solar Cells
